diagnosis: The customer upgraded to the Business tier mid-cycle, resulting in a prorated charge that combines a credit for unused days on the previous plan and a charge for the new plan. This can cause the first invoice total to exceed the standard plan price. No escalation needed; reference internal proration guidelines.
reply:
Hi,

Thanks for reaching out. Because you upgraded to the Business plan on the 14th, your first invoice includes a prorated adjustment for the remaining days of the previous billing period. This means the invoice shows a credit for the unused portion of the old plan and a charge for the new Business plan, which can make the total higher than the listed monthly price. Subsequent invoices will reflect the regular Business plan rate.

If you have any further questions or notice any unexpected line items, please let us know and we’ll be happy to help.

Best regards,
Support Team
